subject.title: fix(msteams): handle bot removal and uninstallation to mark sessions stale

question: For a Microsoft Teams personal app uninstall/remove event, should OpenClaw non-destructively stale only the active DM session, also tombstone cached proactive conversation state, or delete retained transcript/session data?
rationale: The PR touches a privacy and sensitive-history boundary, and the linked issue already frames retention behavior as a maintainer decision; automation can fix mechanics only after the desired retention policy is clear.

options.title: Stale session and tombstone cached conversation state
options.body: Use the existing non-destructive session boundary pattern, clear stale proactive conversation references, and keep transcript deletion out of runtime unless a separate retention policy says otherwise.

options.title: Hard-delete retained Teams DM data
options.body: Treat uninstall as a deletion boundary, but this needs explicit data-loss policy, migration, and stronger security review before implementation.

options.title: Keep only session staling
options.body: Accept the narrowest Discord-like pattern, but cached proactive references may remain a separate privacy/retry concern after uninstall.

recommendation.title: Stale session and tombstone cached conversation state
recommendation.body: Use the existing non-destructive session boundary pattern, clear stale proactive conversation references, and keep transcript deletion out of runtime unless a separate retention policy says otherwise.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Teams security-sensitive and state-store history makes this the best available owner for the retention-boundary decision.
